newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson, Skandia help Swedish shares end at high.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson, Skandia help Swedish shares end at high.

text.p: Swedish shares ended at record high levels on Thursday, fuelled by positive trends on Wall Street and a strong dollar.
The exchange's general index gained 1.21 percent to a record 2,748.45 in turnover of 6.58 billion crowns.
But the bourse was also strong in itself and dealers expected prices to keep rising on strong liquidity.

"If the U.S. falls there is nothing in the current scenario that indicates that the Stockholm bourse will follow," a trader said. "Everything less than an upturn of one percent tomorrow is a disappointment."
Insurer Skandia jumped 14 crowns to 239 crowns in a rebound after slipping three crowns a day earlier when the company released 1996 earnings. Dealers attributed the gain to foreign interest.

Telecoms group Ericsson rose 7.5 crowns to 260 crowns, partly boosted by news it had been selected by India's Reliance Telecom to build a system for a mobile telephone communications along with U.S. firm Motorola.
The forestry sector kept advancing on the strong dollar and ended as the winning sector, up 2.08 percent.
The bank and insurance sector gained 1.69 percent with Swedbank jumping six to 150 and its soon-to-be bride Foreningsbanken gaining 1.40 crowns to 45.60.
Drugs major Astra rose 1.50 crowns to 370 crowns, after testing a new record level of 374 crowns during the day. Rival Pharmacia & Upjohn leaped eight crowns to 293.
